stimulus.source_note: First Charter of Virginia, granted by King James I, April 1606; title page from Select Charters (Macmillan, 1899), public domain.
stimulus.text: The First Charter of Virginia, granted by King James I in April 1606, gave two groups of English investors the right to plant colonies on the American coast. The charter created a joint-stock company: investors bought shares, and the company used the money to pay for ships, supplies, and settlers. The crown kept authority over the colonies and took a share of any gold, silver, or other wealth found.

stem: The First Charter of Virginia was granted by King James I in 1606, and the Spanish crown had divided the Americas by treaty in 1494. What is the most important difference between the English charter and the Spanish-Portuguese treaty as sources of colonial authority?

options.text: The charter was written in English, while the treaty was written in Latin and Spanish
options.misconception: Names a surface difference; the language of a document is not what makes its authority different.

options.text: The charter covered only Virginia, while the treaty covered only Brazil and West Africa
options.misconception: Understates the treaty; it divided all newly discovered lands, not only Brazil.

options.text: The charter granted land to private investors, while the treaty divided lands between two crowns
The charter came from a king, while the treaty came from the pope alone
options.misconception: Overstates the pope's role; the treaty was an agreement between two crowns, with the pope as mediator.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
